companies.name: Amazon Robotics
companies.summary: Amazon operates specialized warehouse robot fleets and DeepFleet orchestration.
companies.placement: Owns warehouse fleet operations and DeepFleet coordination. A broad operational footprint inside one domain, not universal manipulation.
companies.evidenceDetail: Heterogeneous fleet orchestration, not one universal robot policy.

companies.name: Waymo
companies.summary: Waymo develops and deploys a driving system for road vehicles.
companies.placement: Owns a driving service and autonomy in a defined domain. Road-driving intelligence is different from general robot tasks.
companies.evidenceDetail: Road vehicle; no general-purpose manipulation.

companies.name: Agility Robotics
companies.summary: Digit performs tote logistics using a bipedal manipulation platform.
companies.placement: Owns Digit and commercial workflow integration/support. The current evidence centers on material handling despite broader ambition.
companies.evidenceDetail: Bipedal Digit used for tote handling.

companies.name: Ultra
companies.summary: OP1 uses a stationary industrial setup for packing, sorting and kitting, with Physical Intelligence as a model partner.
companies.placement: Shares PI-derived broad-intelligence access, while owning a focused application and customer deployment. Current packaging workflows are bounded; this X position is about the intelligence deployed, not the packaging task alone.
companies.evidenceDetail: Supplied through PI; deployment is on OP1.

companies.name: Dexterity
companies.summary: Mech pairs mobile dual-arm hardware with industrial intelligence and deployment.
companies.placement: Owns Foresight/autonomy and logistics deployment experience. Broad intelligence direction is distinguished from its industrial footprint.
companies.evidenceDetail: Hardware-agnostic direction claimed; logistics footprint better evidenced.

companies.name: Reflex Robotics
companies.summary: A wheeled industrial manipulator combines learned policies with real-time human supervision.
companies.placement: Owns robot and intelligence plus real-time human supervision for delivered industrial work.
companies.evidenceDetail: Mobile manipulation with reach and two arms.

companies.name: Figure
companies.summary: Figure develops its humanoid body and Helix models together.
companies.placement: Owns the body, Helix and Index stack. Broad-task own-body ambition; the cited three-behavior home tests are bounded.
companies.evidenceDetail: Bipedal humanoid with dexterous manipulation.

companies.name: 1X
companies.summary: NEO pairs a humanoid body with model learning from video and robot data.
companies.placement: Owns NEO and robot video/world-model learning with embodiment tuning. Broad home direction does not establish universal cross-body actions.
companies.evidenceDetail: Bipedal humanoid; reported model work covers shorter-horizon behavior.

companies.name: Dyna Robotics
companies.summary: Dyna combines learned manipulation, control and perception with its own wheeled Taku robot.
companies.placement: Owns robot, action model, controller and VLM workflow orchestration. Research spans bodies, but commercial work is focused.
companies.evidenceDetail: Multi-body research demonstrations.

companies.name: Rhoda AI
companies.summary: Rhoda pairs FutureVision with a wheeled industrial robot, using web-video pretraining and robot post-training.
companies.placement: Own video-action intelligence and robot platform. Broad reuse direction; a cited scaling study uses one task, body and setup.
companies.evidenceDetail: Wheeled industrial manipulator.

companies.name: Sunday
companies.summary: Sunday develops ACT models, a capture glove and the wheeled Memo robot.
companies.placement: Owns Memo, ACT and its glove capture system. Household-task ambition with bounded laundry evidence.
companies.evidenceDetail: Wheeled home manipulator.

companies.name: Genesis AI
companies.summary: Genesis combines its GENE model and simulation work with its own Eno robot.
companies.placement: Owns GENE, simulation and Eno. Broad intelligence direction with initial deployments targeted for end-2026.
companies.evidenceDetail: Eno general-purpose robot, announced June 2026.

companies.name: Skild AI
companies.summary: Skild develops S1 for multiple robot bodies and has announced industrial partners and a robotics-automation acquisition.
companies.placement: Broad cross-embodiment S1 direction plus direct deployment responsibility after acquiring Zebra/Fetch. It is no longer adequately described as a pure upstream model supplier.
companies.evidenceDetail: Company demonstrations and portability claims; industrial integration still varies.

companies.name: Field AI
companies.summary: FieldAI develops its own Field Foundation Models and deploys them on customer missions. It describes mission sensor data becoming site reconstructions for simulation training and validation.
companies.placement: Own reusable autonomy plus customer deployment. Navigation and inspection are better evidenced than universal manipulation; this is a field-learning strategy, not a claim of doing everything.
companies.evidenceDetail: The real-to-sim loop is documented. Exclusive customer-data rights and independent proof of compounding advantage are not established.

sources.label: Field deployments → reconstruction → training and validation

companies.name: Physical Intelligence
companies.summary: Physical Intelligence develops general manipulation models and supplies partners including Ultra and Weave.
companies.placement: Upstream robot-action model developer with real task/robot transfer research and named hardware partners. Universal competence remains an ambition.
companies.evidenceDetail: Demonstrated task/robot transfer; universal plug-and-play is not established.

companies.name: Generalist
companies.summary: GEN1.5 explores manipulation with one- or few-shot task adaptation and end-effector transfer.
companies.placement: Upstream own robot foundation-model/capture research with cross-end-effector transfer; not proven universal whole-body autonomy.
companies.evidenceDetail: Demonstrated end-effector transfer; full-body autonomy is a separate question.

companies.name: Reward AI
companies.summary: OM1 targets manipulation across arms and humanoids, alongside capture hardware and low-level control.
companies.placement: Own manipulation-model, capture and control work across arm/humanoid directions. No complete owned humanoid verified.
companies.evidenceDetail: Company-reported across arms and humanoids.

companies.name: Google DeepMind
companies.summary: Gemini Robotics 2 reports a shared VLA checkpoint across Apollo 2 hand variants and Franka Duo.
companies.placement: Flagship-lab robot intelligence is already real: Gemini Robotics 2 VLA, reasoning and on-device variants on partner bodies. Broad reuse is not universal success.
companies.evidenceDetail: Shared VLA checkpoint on Apollo 2 hand variants and Franka Duo.

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.summary: GR00T combines model development with Isaac robotics infrastructure.
companies.placement: Upstream GR00T action-model and infrastructure developer. Cross-body adaptation/post-training is still required.
companies.evidenceDetail: Target-body adaptation and post-training matter.

companies.name: Flexion
companies.summary: Reflect v1 demonstrates partner-humanoid skills including stairs, elevators, doors and parcel handling.
companies.placement: Autonomy on partner humanoids, with broader reuse ambition and a bounded multi-step mission repertoire.
companies.evidenceDetail: Portability claimed; public mission repertoire is bounded.

companies.name: Waddle Labs
companies.summary: Waddle develops partner-arm control where an LLM writes control code and calls vision-language-action models.
companies.placement: Partner-arm agent/control layer combining LLM-written programs and VLA calls. Broad model-independent ambition has limited public demonstrations.
companies.evidenceDetail: Claimed; broad cross-body benchmarking not established.

companies.name: Apptronik
companies.summary: Apollo advertises industrial handling, packing, kitting, inspection and tending.
companies.placement: Own hardware/control/product stack plus access to Gemini robot intelligence. Its broad intelligence direction is separate from bounded data-collection/research work and deployment reliability.
companies.evidenceDetail: Humanoid with bipedal and wheeled configurations.

companies.name: Hadrian
companies.summary: Hadrian develops proprietary Opus and sells precision parts, dedicated manufacturing capacity and factories it operates.
companies.placement: Own Opus factory-autonomy stack and operated production; customers buy manufacturing outcomes. No cross-task, cross-embodiment robot model is established. Underlying pretrained-model provenance is not disclosed.
companies.evidenceDetail: Its customer buys production capacity or a manufactured outcome. This is different from licensing a general robot-action model.

companies.name: Standard Bots
companies.summary: Standard Bots designs and assembles robots and actuators in Glen Cove, New York, and integrates vision, motion, agent software and support.
companies.placement: Own industrial product and customer support, with a manufacturing-task scope. The underlying foundation-model provider is not sufficiently disclosed.
companies.evidenceDetail: American manufacture and integrated software are established. Do not infer an OpenAI robot brain from an investment or partnership association.

companies.name: Boston Dynamics
companies.summary: Boston Dynamics combines its own athletic intelligence with a Google DeepMind partnership for Atlas.
companies.placement: Atlas-specific Gemini intelligence direction plus own athletic control and robot-product responsibility. The partnership is not generalized to Spot or Stretch.
companies.evidenceDetail: The Gemini partnership is Atlas-specific. It does not establish that every Spot or Stretch runs Gemini.

companies.name: Weave
companies.summary: Weave builds its home/laundry robot application using Physical Intelligence models.
companies.placement: Shares PI-derived broad-intelligence access, with own home/laundry application and customer-facing product. It is not placed left because its current workflow is narrow.
companies.evidenceDetail: Named model partnership, not demonstrated ability to swap any model without adaptation.

companies.name: Anthropic
companies.summary: Anthropic has tested Claude in real and simulated robotics and previewed an interface for lab/manufacturing hardware.
companies.placement: Upstream flagship intelligence with actual controller-mediated physical experiments. A released universal low-level action product is not established.
companies.evidenceDetail: July tests perform much better with pretrained low-level policies than direct joint control. August MHS is a research preview for hardware orchestration.

companies.name: OpenAI
companies.summary: OpenAI’s official Robotics team posting describes general-purpose robotics, broad form factors and robotics data infrastructure.
companies.placement: Upstream research/entry evidence rather than a capability coordinate. Shown at the supplier edge; future expansion toward a general action layer is the separate scenario.
companies.evidenceDetail: A team and stated direction are verified. This source does not establish a shipped universal robot-control product.

sources.label: Official Robotics team / data systems role

companies.name: Tacta Systems
companies.summary: Tacta describes its tactile hand, capture glove and manufacturing AI stack.
companies.placement: Manufacturing-focused application/product layer. The underlying physical-AI provider is unnamed, so model provenance and broad-transfer intelligence remain uncertain.
companies.evidenceDetail: Own capture/tactile technology is publicly described. An external PI partnership is not established. Tactum is an unresolved name, not a verified alias.
